ORDER This revision is filed against the Annexure-A5 order, passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kakkanad, in RC 113/2023.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kakkanad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is the de facto complainant in Crime No.678/2022 of Infopark Police Station.
The above case was registered under Sections 405, 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
The police referred the case and submitted a final report.
It is the case of the petitioner that, the learned Magistrate issued a notice to the revision petitioner to appear on 18.06.2024 based on the refer report received.
It is the definite case of the petitioner that, the notice was not served on the revision petitioner before 18.06.2024.
The petitioner received notice only in the morning on 18.06.2024.
Therefore, he was not able to make any arrangement to appear before the learned Magistrate.
The learned 2025:KER:51670 CRL.REV.PET NO.1094 OF 2024 Magistrate,
as per the impugned order, closed the case stating that de facto complainant is absent.
Hence, this revision.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner, Public Prosecutor and also the counsel appearing for the 1 st respondent.
3. This Court perused the impugned order.
In the impugned order, it is stated that "Notice served.
De facto complainant is absent.
Refer case is closed".
According to the petitioner, he has not received notice till 17.06.2024, and he received it only on 18.06.2025.

Considering the facts and the circumstances of the case, I think the impugned order can be set aside and the petitioner should be given an opportunity to file an objection to the refer report in accordance with law.

Therefore, this Criminal Revision Petition is allowed in the following manner:
1.The order dated 18.06.2024 in RC 113/2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kakkanad, is set aside.
